summary.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 58.4% YoY to INR161 crore and PAT 46.1% to INR20.8 crore, with 1,856 MT sold against 2,402 MT produced.
summary.overview: Revenue reached INR161 crore (+58.4% YoY), EBITDA INR31.6 crore (+75.2%) and PAT INR20.8 crore (+46.1%), with a 12.9% PAT margin. The 4,500 MT capacity added at end-FY26 ran at about 90-95% utilisation, taking installed capacity to 11,000 MT. Management said the NCLT approved the merger of two wholly owned subsidiaries effective 21 July 2026, and freeze-dried coffee (FDC) capacity of 5,500 MT is under construction for start in Q2 FY28. Q1 was a seasonal lean quarter, with production exceeding sales and inventory building ahead of Q2 deliveries.

financial_highlights.change: +58.4% YoY vs INR101.6 crore in Q1 FY26
Management figure; analyst calculation of INR172 included chicory

financial_highlights.metric: Capex spent on FDC project to date

segments.name: Spray-dried / agglomerated coffee (core)
segments.commentary: Installed capacity 11,000 MT after 4,500 MT added at end-FY26; packing capacity 5,000 MT; Q1 packing mix 45% bulk and 55% consumer packs. Management guided FY27 volume of about 10,500 MT at 95% utilisation.

segments.name: Chicory (Delecto Foods, wholly owned subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Capacity 2,000 MT per annum; revenue INR42-45 crore per annum; described as profitable and at optimum utilisation with no expansion planned. Management put chicory's Q1 EBITDA at about INR2-2.2 crore and FY27 chicory sales at INR40-45 crore.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue ballpark INR850-900 crore at Q1 average realisation on about 10,500 MT volume (CEO confirmed on call).
Consolidated EBITDA margin expected to improve 0.5-1% from Q1 levels; management cited a 23-24% consolidated EBITDA margin in the business plan for the next two years.
FDC 5,500 MT line to start production in Q2 FY28 after June 2027 trials; FY28 volume from FDC about 2,400 MT at 60-65% utilisation over 8-9 months.
Peak debt capped at INR450 crore; FY28 debt in line with INR400 crore plan. Phase 2 FDC to be funded from incremental FY28 cash flow, with no further equity dilution currently planned.
Management said FY27 operating cash flow would be positive and working capital cycle around 120-125 days.
capex_capacity: Installed capacity: 6,500 MT (January 2025 addition of 2,000 MT) plus 4,500 MT at end-FY26 = 11,000 MT; expansion funded entirely from internal accruals.
Q1 FY27 utilisation: management said the 4,500 MT line ran at about 90-95%, and the plant ran near full capacity after a 15-day annual maintenance shutdown that is already in the capacity figure.
FDC expansion of 5,500 MT on land from Telangana Government Food Processing Zone; total capacity to rise to 16,500 MT. Construction started and advance paid to equipment suppliers.
Another FDC line is likely soon after the first 5,500 MT line is completed.
FDC capex about INR550 crore; INR150 crore spent to date, of which INR25 crore in Q1.
demand_pricing: Green coffee prices stable at about 3,500-3,800 per MT; management expects them to stay in this range through the year, with a healthy Brazil crop offset by weather risk.
Pricing is reset quarterly on a cost-plus basis; management said margin per kg is fixed, so bulk sales lower realisation and EBITDA per kg.
Geography mix: West Africa about 30%, Russia/CIS about 22%, Southeast Asia about 20%, Central America about 15%, Europe about 10%, India about 5%.
Customers: about 90% direct brand owners and about 10% traders. Management cited about 98% customer retention.

FDC: management cited LOIs for 70-80% of FDC capacity from Russia, Europe, the US and Southeast Asia (subject to quality and price). Two of these customers are new and five are existing. Global FDC market is about 2,50,000 MT, so 5,500 MT is about 2.2% share.
FDC realisation expected to be 28-32% above spray-dried, which management said is equivalent to a 20-30% EBITDA per kg premium in later exchanges.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 4,500 MT capacity contributing revenue in Q1, and what is its utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Commissioned in March 2026 and running at about 90-95% utilisation in Q1; Q1 is seasonally lean, with Q2-Q4 expected to improve.

qa_highlights.question: Will EBITDA margins keep rising, and what is the FDC start timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin expected to rise 0.5-1% from Q1 levels. FDC trials by June 2027 with production from Q2 FY28; 60-65% utilisation over 8-9 months, adding about 2,400 MT in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 revenue potential and the chicory contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the FY27 revenue ballpark is INR850-900 crore on 10,500 MT. Chicory revenue is INR40-45 crore a year, and EBITDA from chicory in Q1 was about INR2.1 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What are the debt and capex plans for FDC?
qa_highlights.answer: Peak debt capped at INR450 crore; phase 2 to be funded from FY28 incremental cash flow; no equity dilution planned at present.

qa_highlights.question: Why are working capital days high at 120-130 and when does cash flow improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth inventory is the main reason; CFO said FY27 operating cash flow will be positive, with working capital days around 125 and the FY27 cash-generation capacity estimated at about INR79 crore if growth inventory was not needed.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any hedging or inventory loss risk given production above sales in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said beans are bought back-to-back, with 40-45 days of stock held; surplus Q1 production is expected to be picked up by customers in Q2.

risks_watch: FDC ramp-up: 5,500 MT line depends on June 2027 trials, with production from Q2 FY28 and FY28 volume of about 2,400 MT at 60-65% utilisation over 8-9 months; LOIs cover 70-80% of capacity but are subject to quality and price.

Pricing and inventory: prices are reset quarterly on cost-plus; Q1 production of 2,402 MT exceeded sales of 1,856 MT, so Q2 offtake of surplus stock and the back-to-back bean hedge (40-45 days stock) need to hold.
Margin trajectory: management guided a 0.5-1% EBITDA margin uplift from Q1 levels and a 23-24% consolidated margin in the business plan; bulk mix and FDC mix could dilute EBITDA per kg.

Working capital and cash: 120-130 day cycle, FY27 operating cash flow guided positive, peak debt capped at INR450 crore; Phase 2 FDC funding relies on FY28 incremental cash flow with no equity dilution currently planned.

Chicory and EBITDA per kg reconciliation: management's Q1 EBITDA per kg of INR157 differs from the INR172 analyst calculation on the INR32 crore EBITDA base; disclosure of volume and per-kg figures in press releases was requested by an analyst.
key_quotes: Quarter 1 is the lean period, but it will start improving from the second quarter onwards.
Ours is a cost-plus margin. So, obviously, we have fixed profits on a per-kg basis.
We always procure the coffee beans on a back-to-back basis.
Because our customer retention is almost 98%. For the last so many years, they have been with us.
summary.management_tone: Confident on volumes, capacity and the FY27 revenue ballpark, but cautious and often deferential on pricing and per-kg economics, repeatedly saying realisation depends on quarterly price resets. Evasive on the FDC market share and sales-force build-out, and on the EBITDA-per-kg and FY28 consolidated margin questions, where the CFO deferred ("we'll be sharing at the later stage").
